summary: Provides a framework for using Path Computation Elements to do inter-layer traffic engineering in MPLS and GMPLS networks. It looks at optimizing resources across all layers together rather than separately. It is informational.

eli5.summary: A city has roads, rail and air. Planning each alone wastes effort, so this suggests one planner looking at all of them together.

questions: single pce vs multiple pce path computation
subtitle: How Path Computation Elements can plan routes across packet and optical layers, and how new lower-layer links get set up.

tldr.problem: A network can have several layers, such as packet over optical, and planning each layer on its own wastes resources; a higher-layer node often cannot see the lower layer, so a path across it may fail to compute.
tldr.mechanism: The framework describes three PCE path computation models (single PCE, multiple PCEs with or without inter-PCE communication) and three ways to control the lower-layer connections that form the Virtual Network Topology.
tldr.outcome: It defines no new protocol. It offers guidance on choosing models and discusses stability, manageability and security trade-offs for operators.

today: RFC 5623 is an Informational framework from September 2009, and the metadata shows it has not been obsoleted or updated. It defines no protocol itself and builds on RFC 4655.

sections.title: Multi-Layer Networks and Inter-Layer Traffic Engineering
sections.content:
A network may have several layers, split by technology (for example packet switch capable, time division multiplex or lambda switch capable), by switching granularity, or by client and server roles. Label Switched Paths (LSPs) in a lower layer carry higher-layer LSPs across the lower-layer network. The topology formed by lower-layer LSPs advertised as traffic engineering links (TE links) in the higher layer is the Virtual Network Topology (VNT).

Optimizing across all layers instead of each alone is called inter-layer traffic engineering. It covers computing end-to-end paths across layers and controlling the VNT by setting up and releasing lower-layer LSPs. It falls within the PCE-based architecture of RFC 4655, and this document is a framework for applying that to MPLS and GMPLS.
sections.eli5: When a network has layers, like roads over rail, planning them together uses everything better. The rail links you build can then show up as new roads on the road map.

sections.title: Inter-Layer Path Computation
sections.content:
The RFC's running example has a higher layer (LSRs H1 to H4) and a lower optical layer (H2, L1, L2, H3). H1 wants a path to H4, but there is no TE link between the border LSRs H2 and H3, and H1 cannot see the lower layer. A single-layer computation fails. An inter-layer computation can answer with the route H1-H2-H3-H4 and suggest a lower-layer LSP H2-L1-L2-H3.

The PCE can return one of two kinds of result, converted into an Explicit Route Object for RSVP-TE signaling:

  • Mono-layer path. Only same-layer TE links. It may use existing lower-layer LSPs, virtual TE links not yet established (signaling triggers their setup), or a loose hop across the lower layer that a border LSR expands itself or with a PCE.
  • Multi-layer path. Includes TE links from distinct layers, covering the whole path of lower-layer LSPs that exist or are still to be created.
sections.eli5: The planner can say go from stop A to B and let the rail office pick the tracks, or it can name every track itself.

sections.title: Three Path Computation Models
sections.content:
Three models come from RFC 4655.

  • Single PCE. One multi-layer PCE sees all layers and can compute the whole path, for example H1-H2-L1-L2-H3-H4. It needs more computation power and memory, but can be faster because no PCE-to-PCE messages are exchanged, and it suits cases where all layers' topology is visible within one routing domain.
  • Multiple PCE with inter-PCE communication. Each layer has its own mono-layer PCE and they collaborate. In the example, the higher-layer PCE picks H2 and H3 as border points, asks the lower-layer PCE for H2 to H3, receives H2-L1-L2-H3, and returns the full path. This keeps layer boundaries and keeps each topology database smaller.
  • Multiple PCE without inter-PCE communication. Separate computations are made independently for the head end and each border LSR entering a new layer.

With several candidate border nodes, a single PCE can examine them all easily. For cooperating PCEs, the backward-recursive techniques of RFC 5441 could be used by treating layers as separate domains.
sections.eli5: You can have one planner who knows both roads and rail, two planners who phone each other, or two planners who never talk and each plan their own part.

sections.title: Controlling the Virtual Network Topology
sections.content:
A VNT Manager (VNTM) manages and controls the VNT. It is separate from the PCE, though they may be collocated. Four path control models are described.

  • PCE-VNTM cooperation. When computation fails for lack of a TE link, the PCE suggests to the VNTM that a lower-layer LSP be created. The VNTM applies policy and asks an ingress LSR such as H2 to set it up. H2 advertises it as a TE link and the PCE recomputes and replies with H1-H2-H3-H4. If the PCE waits, it must operate a timeout.
  • Higher-layer signaling trigger. The PCE returns a path including the unestablished lower-layer route, or a loose hop. The border LSR, on receiving the higher-layer signaling message, applies local policy and sets up the lower-layer LSP, using hierarchical signaling from RFC 4206.
  • NMS-VNTM cooperation, integrated flavor. The network management system asks the PCE, then works with the VNTM to have the lower-layer LSP set up.
  • NMS-VNTM cooperation, separate flavor. The head-end reports failure to the NMS, which asks the VNTM, which uses a lower-layer PCE. This is a point for administrative, billing and security policy.
sections.eli5: If the planner finds a missing rail link, it can tell a rail manager to build one, or let the station build it when a train arrives, or ask the office staff to arrange it.

sections.title: Choosing a Model and Operational Concerns
sections.content:
Table 1 of the RFC shows which combinations of computation and control models are possible. The PCE-VNTM and signaling trigger models work with all three computation models. The integrated NMS-VNTM flavor does not fit multiple PCE without inter-PCE communication, and the separate flavor fits only that model (for a single PCE, the PCE function may be collocated but operates on separate databases).

Choosing between control models depends on several factors. Cooperation models need VNTM functions and extra communication steps, which gives better control at the cost of longer setup time. The signaling trigger model needs no VNTM but needs added border LSR functions, and the ingress LSR must tolerate longer setup because lower-layer signaling occurs during higher-layer signaling. Where operators want clear separation between layers, the VNTM is a natural coordination point for policy and billing.

Stability is a concern. A very large lower-layer LSP might be set up for a small, possibly short-lived demand, and cycles of rerouting and deletion can make the network unstable. The RFC suggests policy and configuration limits, such as threshold parameters giving hysteresis. Other sections cover manageability: configuration switches for inter-layer computation, per-layer and inter-layer policy, MIB support, and liveness monitoring.
sections.eli5: Which way is best depends on who runs what. Do not build a giant rail line for one tiny trip, and do not tear it down and rebuild it again and again.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Inter-layer traffic engineering with PCE raises new security issues in all three control models. In the PCE-VNTM model, the communications should ensure authenticity, privacy and integrity, mainly to prevent false triggers that could tie up lower-layer resources, amounting to denial of service, or cause incorrect billing. SNMPv3 should be used where PCE MIB modules carry the notifications.

In the signaling trigger model the main concern is confidentiality, since the PCC may not be trusted with lower-layer topology. Options are a loose hop or masking the lower-layer path with a path key (RFC 5520). The NMS-VNTM model moves security issues into the management plane, where authentication of operators and policy is needed. A single PCE with full visibility means one breach can expose all layers' topology, and instability from inter-layer TE could be exploited to attack either layer.
sections.eli5: Whoever can fake a request to build a rail link could waste the rail company's resources. A planner who knows every layer is also a juicy target.
